evidence.text: The character entry identifies 明 as U+660E and gives its current Mandarin reading as míng.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 明

evidence.field: 囧 component record; pronunciation reports and graphic account
evidence.text: The entry describes 囧 as a perforated window and reports the Shuowen pronunciations 讀若獷 and, from Jia Shi Zhong, 讀與明同. These are historical lexicographic reports; the entry does not establish the spoken name of the depicted window or prove that it matched 明 in sound.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 囧 component analysis

evidence.field: 甲骨文及金文用例；early forms and senses
evidence.text: The entry reports 日+月 forms associated with dawn or brightness, as well as 月+囧 forms interpreted as moonlight entering through a perforated window. It cites oracle-bone examples for dawn (合集481) and brightness (合集21037); it also reports 目+月 and 田+月 forms, with the identification of 目+月 uncertain and 田 possibly a corruption of 日 or 囧. Qin Shuihudi’s 目-form is reported as a likely corruption of 囧. The entry also reports later bronze uses meaning clear or manifest. These are the database’s readings and interpretations; the cited artifact images were not inspected.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 明

evidence.text: The description identifies 明-oracle.svg as a digital vector depiction of 明 in Shang oracle-script style, points to source collections and a specific Hanziyuan record, and labels the rendering public domain. It is a modern digital rendering, not an artifact photograph. The description page exposes the original file link, but fetching the image returned HTTP 429; its pixels were not inspected.

gaps: The official character-specific Unihan pages for U+660E and U+56E7 could not be opened. Current readings are therefore not verified through the requested Unicode click-through records in this pass. CUHK confirms 明 míng; its 囧 component record does not provide a directly readable modern Mandarin syllable in the inspected text.

No historical glyph image is selected: the Commons description page establishes the candidate’s identity and rights, but the original image request returned HTTP 429. No alternate character-specific image with verified direct URL and reuse provenance was established in this pass.
The CUHK account reports oracle-bone attestations of both dawn and brightness, but their relative chronology is unresolved. Exact artifact dates and underlying inscription images were not checked.

The reported 囧 phonetic role in 月+囧 is not independently demonstrated here. The historical report that 囧 was read like 明 does not recover the ancient spoken name of the depicted window; no sound relationship should be inferred from the depiction alone.

limitations.text: No image candidate is included because the only inspected candidate’s exact original image URL returned HTTP 429, and no alternate candidate with verified identity and reuse provenance was established. The Commons page describes a modern vector rendering in Shang oracle-script style, not an ancient artifact photograph.
